chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, there is a rank for the servant with Allah that he does not attain except by one of two traits: either by the loss of his wealth or by an affliction in his body.

key_terms.جَسَدِهِ: his body, meaning physical condition or health
key_terms.ذَهَابِ مَالِهِ: the loss or departure of his wealth
key_terms.مَنْزِلَةٌ: a rank or station of honor with Allah

ai.seo_question: How can loss of wealth or physical affliction raise a believer's rank with Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a servant may have a special rank with Allah that is only reached through trial and hardship. It highlights that loss of wealth or bodily affliction can be means by which a believer is elevated spiritually.
